steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (She's insane! Absolutely insane! That's an entire district of people we're talking about!)

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (Besides, does she really think she can come away clean from an incident of this scale?)

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (If I went along with her plan, I'd be the first one to take the fall!)

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (Even though I'm losing this opportunity, there's nothing to feel bad about. I'll have other opportunities... I can afford to wait!)

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (I made it... to Vyseheim's customs office...)
Just as Ebenholz is about to enter the customs office, an intense headache nearly knocks him off his feet.

steps.name: Voice from Nowhere
steps.text: A coward on the run...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I don't need you telling me what to do!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Even if I die in Urtica, I don't want to become a murderer like you!

steps.name: Voice from Nowhere
steps.text: You fear... You are afraid!

steps.name: Voice from Nowhere
steps.text: If you are ensnared by fear... then never in your life shall you taste freedom!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Shut up!

steps.name: Voice from Nowhere
steps.text: Naive idiot...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Call me whatever you want...

steps.name: Voice from Nowhere
steps.text: Do you think that woman can get you out of here so easily?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (Good, it doesn't look like there's anyone here...)

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (I just need to be extra-careful and make sure nobody sees me...)

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (Just a little farther, and I'll be in the uninhabited plate on the edge of the city...)

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (Takes a deep breath)

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Were you seriously planning to jump off the edge of a nomadic city?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: While that is technically the quickest way out of Vyseheim, I would advise against it.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Don't force my hand, Gertrude.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I have no intention of doing that.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Then leave me alone, and get out of my sight.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Where do you plan to go?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Vyseheim will continue to move until the concert comes to an end. You have nowhere to go.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Even if you risk life and limb to force your way out, only the barren wastelands await you.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'd rather...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...step into the uncharted wastelands than...

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: You'd rather die in the wastes than spend another second in Vyseheim?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Correct.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I understand how you feel, but can you calm down first and let me finish?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What more do I need to hear from you?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Do you really want me to reveal everything to you right here, my dear Graf Urtica?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Graf Urtica...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You don't need to emphasize my title. I know what you're trying to say.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: First of all, I promise that under the current conditions, our plan can still proceed smoothly.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: It's not 'our' plan, it's yours.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: If your semantic games allow you to sleep better at night, then so be it.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Kreide's Voice of Mundane is damaged, and Rhodes Island has also discovered its side effect.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Can a damaged Voice of Mundane cancel out another one? Even if it could, would Rhodes Island turn a blind eye?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Indeed, Kreide's Voice of Mundane can still join in Resonanz.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: As for Rhodes Island... Where do you think we are?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: This is Vyseheim. My domain.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: That little Fräulein Hibiscus is also an Infected. Even letting her step into Leithanien is only to keep up appearances with Rhodes Island. She can go nowhere but Vyseheim.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: In any case, she only knows that there's something going on with you and Kreide, but doesn't know how it's happening. She has no evidence.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I understand, you don't have the heart to bring harm upon the Infected who have nothing to do with this.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: The way I see it, this compassion is extraneous. But if you truly wish to act upon it, it is even more important that you carry out the plan.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Carry out the plan, and let all those Infected people die?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I'll tell you the rest of the plan then.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: You and Kreide will duet, and you will remove your own Voice of Mundane.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Afterwards, I'll create some commotion in the concert hall, and take advantage of the chaos to kill Kreide and disguise his body as yours––

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What did you say?!

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: As he has become the biggest scourge of the Afterglow, it is impossible for him to live on.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Impossible for what? Don't be ridiculous! The biggest scourge of the Afterglow is none other than YOU!

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: As I said before, all the scourges of the Afterglow come from Kreide's corrupted Voice of Mundane.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Resonanz exacerbates the leakage of the Voice of Mundane, in an irreversible process.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Even if you were to plummet off the edge of this nomadic city, Kreide's Voice of Mundane would not return to the relatively harmless state it was in a week ago.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: More importantly, the Voice of Mundane isn't just harming the people around Kreide, it's also hurting him.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: He is the biggest victim of the Resonanz between you two.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: He may seem perfectly healthy right now, but don't be fooled. That is just another example of false recovery.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Kreide's body may have adapted to the Voice of Mundane in the past, but with the recent surge of leakage, this delicate balance is about to be thrown upside down.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: An optimistic estimate is that his good days will come to an end within two weeks. After that, he will experience the intense suffering that occurs in the acute phase following the false recovery phase.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: The happiest ending for both him and the Afterglow, would be for him to die following the concert.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: For you, for me, for the Afterglow, and for him. It would be a good thing.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: I would obtain a trump card I could pull out at any time. The Afterglow would obtain peace, Kreide would obtain his rest.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: And you... you would obtain your freedom.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Graf Urtica, rightful heir to Leithanien...

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: The last of the Witch King's bloodline.
Freedom.
For as long as I can remember, I've never known freedom.
Poor child.
No courtesy or greetings are needed. Just listen to me.
Even though you were born into a distant branch far from the Witch King, you are indeed the last of his bloodline.
Out of pity, I will not trouble you.
Beyond that, you shall also inherit the fiefs passed down from generation to generation in your family.
You will become the Lehnsherr of Urtica.
You will learn to take responsibility for your own subjects.
You are about to take a completely different path from that of your disgraceful kin––
I await you.
This was my first memory.

I was around five or six years old at the time, I can't remember from before that. I only vaguely remember coming into contact with a strange thing called the 'Voice of Mundane,' and nearly lost my life.
Staring at the pure-white dress in front of me, I was filled with thoughts that I'd become some obscure little aristocrat.
I thought I'd live the rest of my life in peace, with the exception of the occasional headache and the auditory hallucinations from the Voice of Mundane.

steps.name: Stoic-Looking Noble
steps.text: Your Illustrious Highness, you should know to mind your words and actions, and to not leave the Spire without good reason.

steps.name: Stoic-Looking Noble
steps.text: I must remind you, everything that you are has been bestowed upon you by Their Majesties.

steps.name: Cautious Servant
steps.text: Your Illustrious Highness, aren't you forgetting something?

steps.name: Cautious Servant
steps.text: You ought to praise Their Majesties before you eat.

steps.name: Rule-Abiding Instructor
steps.text: Your Illustrious Highness, we will be learning a new piece today.

steps.name: Rule-Abiding Instructor
steps.text: This song expresses the gratitude of the nobles towards Their Majesties. Please keep that in your heart.

steps.name: Mediocre Caster
steps.text: Your Illustrious Highness, your mastery over Originium Arts is simply transcendent!

steps.name: Mediocre Caster
steps.text: Hm, you want something more elaborate? Haha, you need not wear yourself out.
Everyone around me did everything they could to limit my freedom, instilling in my mind an allegiance to the Twin Empresses.
If that was the price for being able to live in peace and quiet, I was willing to pay it.
I paid it for a very long time.

steps.name: Stoic-Looking Noble
steps.text: Your Illustrious Highness, I shall be frank from the onset. You are the true heir to Leithanien.

steps.name: Stoic-Looking Noble
steps.text: I've been laying in wait in your spire for a number of years now. I'm sure you recognize me.

steps.name: Stoic-Looking Noble
steps.text: You don't have to say anything. Just listen to me. You don't have to agree with me or repudiate me.

steps.name: Stoic-Looking Noble
steps.text: I know that you're scared, that you don't want to lose even this life you have now. But you should at least know how those people see you, and what they want you to do.

steps.name: Stoic-Looking Noble
steps.text: I'm sure you know that the attendants the tyrants have forced upon you are setting up the banquet below. I will take you there, and let you see the truth.
The one in front of me grabbed me and pulled me up off the ground.
My palm was drenched in sweat.

steps.name: Uproarious Voice
steps.text: Now that's the good stuff!

steps.name: Uproarious Voice
steps.text: I had no idea you had such exquisite wine down in the cellar.

steps.name: Familiar Voice
steps.text: You flatter me.

steps.name: Familiar Voice
steps.text: Urtica's countryside lacks just about everything, but there are indeed a number of master winemakers here.

steps.name: Uproarious Voice
steps.text: Then we've got to make sure to drink our fill before the little runt grows up. Can't be leaving any for him!

steps.name: Familiar Voice
steps.text: Haha, that simply won't do.

steps.name: Familiar Voice
steps.text: The boy has been under house arrest for a number of years, but I'm looking for the right time to teach him how to drink. I'll have to fill him until he's a hopeless alcoholic.
I was entranced for a short while.

a.text: 'You will become the Lehnsherr of Urtica.'

steps.name: Uproarious Voice
steps.text: Oh, so you still had that trick up your sleeves.

steps.name: Uproarious Voice
steps.text: Once the runt has been completely soaked with wine, it'll be a load off Their Majesties'––

steps.name: Familiar Voice
steps.text: Shh!

steps.name: Uproarious Voice
steps.text: Yes, yes, right. Screw me, mate! Guess I'll have to repent with another glass!

a.text: 'You will learn to take responsibility for your own subjects.'

steps.name: Familiar Voice
steps.text: But remember, these words don't leave the wine table.

steps.name: Familiar Voice
steps.text: We can't allow the boy to have heirs. That's the order from on high, with my life on the line.

steps.name: Uproarious Voice
steps.text: If it's that big of a deal, why don't you find an apothecary...

steps.name: Familiar Voice
steps.text: That won't work, it'd leave a paper trail. Only by letting him usher his own downfall will my task be considered complete.

steps.name: Uproarious Voice
steps.text: Ambitious! Truly ambitious! Come, let us drink to that!

a.text: 'You are about to take a completely different path from that of your disgraceful kin––'

steps.name: Familiar Voice
steps.text: If I can get rid of the boy without getting my hands dirty, then Urtica will be mine.

steps.name: Uproarious Voice
steps.text: I'll drink to that! Prost!

steps.name: Familiar Voice
steps.text: Prost!

steps.name: Voice from Nowhere
steps.text: Haha, hahahahaha....

steps.name: Voice from Nowhere
steps.text: Did you hear that, boy?

steps.name: Voice from Nowhere
steps.text: This is the peaceful, easygoing life you wanted!

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Herr Ebenholz, Herr Ebenholz?

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: You fell over on the spot. I almost had you sent to the hospital.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Feeling a little better?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'm perfectly fine.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: About the plan...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I don't want to hear it right now.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'm going.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: As I said, you can leave at any time.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Don't come pestering me again.

steps.name: Gertrude
steps.text: Well, you'll have to forgive me for being bad at following orders.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Welcome back–– Your complexion looks terrible. What's wrong, did you get sick?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'm fine.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: You sure don't look fine to me. Go rest in bed and I'll boil some water for you.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: There's no need.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Relax. I used to take care of Grandpa when he first got sick. Just lie down and let me handle the rest.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: If you don't get any better, I'm going to tell Hibiscus.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I'll be right back!
Graf Urtica endures a splitting headache and lies there in bed.
His consciousness gradually blurs.

steps.name: Voice from Nowhere
steps.text: Depraved maggots.

steps.name: Voice from Nowhere
steps.text: They would destroy your exalted bloodline...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Shut up...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Argh!

steps.name: Voice from Nowhere
steps.text: Self-deprecating trash!
The sound of a cello comes from afar.
His headache is no less intense, but the voice in Graf Urtica's head is drowned out by the melody from the cello.
A wave of reprieve washes over him.
This melody sounds somewhat familiar.
His splitting headache makes it impossible for him to gather his thoughts, but he feels he has heard this melody somewhere before.
Where have I heard this before...
Where?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: You're awake!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Just stay put for now. Hibiscus just came over and drew blood when she saw the state you were in. She said there's nothing wrong with your body, but you might be over-stressed and worn out.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (Over-stressed... Hah...)

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I heard someone playing the cello just now... Was that you?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Where... did you learn that melody?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Hmm, maybe someone hummed it to me when I was little?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I don't exactly remember.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: When you were little...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: When you were little––

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You–– You're that––

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I'm what?
The weakened Graf Urtica struggles a few times, but nevertheless is unable to crawl out of bed.
But those dusty memories within his mind, awakened by the sound of the cello, flashed once more before his eyes.
